propositions: Git fetch to GitHub mirror intermittently hangs past 320s due to byte-starved connections not being aborted by throughput thresholds, only by the 300s wall-clock timeout.
The git argv in _fetch_origin lacks http.lowSpeedLimit and http.lowSpeedTime config, so curl has no mechanism to abort on zero-byte-per-second stalls independent of wall time.
A stalled fetch (connection accepted, zero bytes transferred) must abort in ~10 seconds via throughput-keyed config rather than burning the full 300s budget.
A legitimately slow but progressing fetch (e.g., 2000 B/s sustained) must not be aborted; the abort threshold must be keyed on throughput rate, not elapsed time.
Transient low-speed aborts should be retried in-process a bounded number of times to self-heal within a single review, while non-low-speed failures (auth, bad ref) must not be retried.
